title: Physical or pseudo device?
description: Sort device files by whether real hardware stands behind them or only kernel code.

items.why: The first SATA, SCSI or USB disk: a real storage device.
No hardware at all: reading gives nothing at once and everything written is thrown away.
The first NVMe SSD, a real drive.
Only kernel code: reading gives an endless stream of zero bytes.
The first optical drive (CD, DVD or Blu-ray).
It produces random bytes in software, with no device behind it.
The first partition on the disk `sda`. It is a part of a real disk.
Disks get letters in the order the kernel finds them, so a USB stick plugged in later can become `sdb`.
The second partition of the first NVMe drive.

items.text: The device file you redirect to with `command > /dev/null` to silence output.
items.why: It is the "black hole" `/dev/null`: no hardware, only the kernel throwing the data away.
